title: Chinese demo
description: Sample of Mandarin Chinese support: pinyin over characters, the Pinyin and Tone colours switches, pinyin typing with tone numbers, read-aloud in Chinese, tone questions and tone practice, and the Simplified/Traditional switch.

lessons.title: Hello and thank you
lessons.body:
## Characters and pinyin

Each character is one syllable. **Pinyin** above it shows the sound and the tone: {你好|nǐ hǎo} (hello), {谢谢|xiè xie} (thank you; the second syllable has the neutral tone, so no mark).

> *{你好|nǐ hǎo}！{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng}。* — Hello! I'm a student.

| Characters | Pinyin | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| {中国|Zhōng guó} | Zhōngguó | China |
| {一点儿|yì diǎnr} | yìdiǎnr | a little |

A line break inside a paragraph joins Chinese text without a space:
{我|wǒ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}
{喝|hē}{茶|chá}。

## Tones

Mandarin has four tones and a neutral tone: {妈|mā} (mother), {麻|má} (hemp), {马|mǎ} (horse), {骂|mà} (to scold), {吗|ma} (question word). Turn on **Tone colours** to colour each syllable by its tone.

Two third tones in a row: the first is said as a second tone ({你好|nǐ hǎo} sounds like ní hǎo). Tone questions accept both. After this lesson, **Practise the tones** drills the words you learned by ear.

## Writing characters

Trace each character stroke by stroke, in mainland (PRC) stroke order. Start at number 1 and follow the arrow. {={学|xué}=} is written {+{学|xué}+} in traditional characters; both trace.

```trace
人 你 好 们 学 學
```

lessons.title: Simplified and traditional
lessons.body:
## Two scripts

This course is written in simplified characters. The **Simplified / Traditional** switch shows all of it in traditional characters (Taiwan forms); the pinyin stays the same: {头发|tóu fa} (hair), {面条|miàn tiáo} (noodles), {一只猫|yì zhī māo} (a cat), {这里|zhè lǐ} (here), {台湾|Tái wān} (Taiwan).

New character: simplified {={学|xué}=} · traditional {+{学|xué}+} (to study).

{=
### About the simplified form

This section always stays in simplified characters, because it describes them: 学 has 8 strokes, and its top is written ⺍. One simplified 发 stands for two traditional characters (hair and to send). A trace block follows the learner's script even here:

```trace
学国
```
=}

questions.explanation: {谢谢|xiè xie}: the second syllable is neutral.

questions.stem: Type “hello” in pinyin with tone numbers (ni3hao3 becomes nǐhǎo): ___
questions.explanation: {你好|nǐ hǎo}: both syllables are tone 3 (spoken ní hǎo).

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {谢谢|xiè xie}: a falling fourth tone, then the neutral tone.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: Written 3+3; you hear 2+3 (third-tone sandhi). Either answer counts.

questions.stem: In traditional characters, which form does {=发=} take in {=头发=} (hair)?
questions.explanation: {=髮=} is hair; {=發=} is to send or to start, as in {=出发 / 出發=} (to set off).

glossary.definition: The official romanization of Mandarin: {拼音|pīn yīn}, with a tone mark over each syllable.
